Miss O'Neill, a waitress at St. Stephen's Club, of which Mr. Newton was a member, said that when Mr. Newton arrived on Easter Saturday he seemed very ill. On Sunday night he called her to him and said: "I think I will finish it in a taxi to night." She asked what he meant, and he took a revolver from his pocket and said: "This is what I mean." She asked him to think it over until the morning and let her have the revolver. Mr. Newton replied: "No, I mean to finish it to night." He asked her to notice his suit, saying, "What do you think I am wearing an old suit for?"
TOOK MORPHIA
Miss O'Neill added that Mr. Newton said that he took morphia a few nights before and was surprised it did not finish him. He got up and remarked, "Good luck and a jolly good shot." He kept the revolver in his pocket and seemed it a "don't care" mood.

text: ATTACK BY MASKED MAN

label: text
text:
Mrs. Doig, wife of a bank clerk, who lives near St. Albans, was brutally attacked by a man in her house and probably owes her life to her presence of mind, in feigning death. "After my husband had gone," she told a reporter, "a man whom I found in the hall clutched me by the throat and threw me to the ground. He belaboured me with a long cudgel, beating me about the head and body. In my arms I held Peter my little 14-month-old sop, and I expected him to be killed every second. The more I screamed the more the man hit me, so I pretended to be dead, lying perfectly still. A moment later the man stopped, and then I fainted and remembered nothing more till I found he had gone."
